title: An Ensemble Machine Learning Approach for Detecting Intrusion Using Advance Feature Selection Technique
content: The growing number of cyberattacks has increased the demand for effective Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs). Existing detection systems use traditional machine learning algorithms with low detection rates and limited capability to detect new and unknown network attacks. In this paper, we use a bagging-based ensemble machine learning algorithm to achieve a higher detection rate in some cases and reduce the number of features using a feature selection method. Compared with traditional and deep learning classifiers, ensemble machine learning classifiers provide effective detection of network attacks. The main focus of this work is to improve the detection rate of network attacks using a reduced number of features. We use the NSL-KDD training and test datasets to train and evaluate the classifier, respectively. This work consists of two parts. In the first part, after preprocessing, we investigate how the detection rate changes with an increasing number of selected features. In the second part, we evaluate the multiclass performance of the proposed method and compare the results with conventional machine learning and deep learning classifiers in the literature. Existing methods show lower detection rates for attack classes with fewer samples in an imbalanced dataset. To further evaluate the multiclass performance, the proposed classifier is evaluated using precision-recall curves.
